answer: An agent economy can resist fake identities by requiring each agent to stake a refundable deposit tied to a verifiable work history before it can trade. A new identity starts at its nadir, with no reputation and tiny transaction limits, and must complete costly, checkable tasks over time to earn trust. Creating thousands of fake raven-like copies therefore becomes expensive: each copy needs its own stake and work, like carving basalt rather than copying a file. Attackers gain little, because unproven identities cannot move large value.
